derivation: Source file has 2,555,085 data rows (2,555,086 lines including header; md5 9b318b5a277ea80de32eb913490d1bd2 verified against the FTP meta.yaml). Dropped 5,766 rows with no usable chromosome (5,765 rows had hm_chrom=NA because harmonisation could not map the variant, 1 row had hm_chrom=MT; the table covers chrom 1-22 and X only). Of the remaining 2,549,319 rows, dropped 18,464 more that had neither a usable hm_beta nor hm_odds_ratio (this study reports betas only: hm_odds_ratio is NA for every one of the 2,555,085 rows in the file, so the OR-to-beta fallback ln(OR) was never triggered), leaving 2,530,855 rows usable for beta-requiring tables. Thinning: kept all 21,813 of those with p<1e-3, plus a seeded (numpy default_rng, seed 20150212) random sample of the remaining 2,509,042 rows. A 2% bulk sample (the SPEC.md default) produced a 3,904,189-byte file, over the 2 MB cap, so the bulk rate was reduced to 0.55%, giving 13,636 sampled rows (2,495,406 dropped) and a final file of 35,449 rows / 1,964,245 bytes. The X chromosome has only 6 variants in the whole file; none had p<1e-3 and none were hit by the 0.55% sample, so no X rows appear in the final table even though X is a valid chromosome in the pipeline. Numeric columns are written with %.6g formatting to avoid pandas surfacing float64 round-trip noise (for example 2.287e-40 rendering as 2.2869999999999998e-40); the source file never carries more than 4-6 significant figures for these fields.
thinning: Keep every variant with p < 0.001 (21813 rows), plus a seeded sample (numpy default_rng(seed=20260925)) of 4000 of the other 13636 rows of the source table, which is itself a seeded sample of the full summary statistics. The kept rows keep the source order. The copy drops the columns beta, se, which no gallery chart reads.

columns.expected_neg_log10_p: expected -log10(p) under the null: -log10(rank/(n+1)), ranked over all 2,555,085 p-values in the file sorted ascending, rounded to 4 decimal places
columns.observed_neg_log10_p: observed -log10(p) for the corresponding sorted p-value, rounded to 4 decimal places
columns.ci_lower: lower bound of the 95% confidence band on expected_neg_log10_p: -log10 of the 0.975 quantile of Beta(rank, n-rank+1), the null distribution of the rank-th order statistic of n uniform(0,1) draws, rounded to 4 decimal places
columns.ci_upper: upper bound of the 95% confidence band on expected_neg_log10_p: -log10 of the 0.025 quantile of the same Beta(rank, n-rank+1) distribution, rounded to 4 decimal places

derivation: Computed on ALL 2,555,085 p-values in the file (0 were NA, 0, or outside (0,1], so none were dropped for the QQ/lambda computation). Sorted ascending; expected=-log10(rank/(n+1)), observed=-log10(p_sorted) — the standard QQ-plot formula. The 95% confidence band (ci_lower, ci_upper) uses the order-statistic distribution: the rank-th smallest of n uniform(0,1) draws follows Beta(rank, n-rank+1) under the null, computed with scipy.stats.beta.ppf(0.975, rank, n-rank+1) and scipy.stats.beta.ppf(0.025, rank, n-rank+1) on the same rank used for expected_neg_log10_p, then -log10-transformed with the quantiles flipped (the 0.975 p-value quantile gives the lower -log10 bound; the 0.025 quantile gives the upper one), all on the full untihinned rank set. Genomic inflation factor lambda_GC = median(chi-square from p, 1 df) / qchisq(0.5, 1) = 1.111615383472537, also computed on the full untihinned p-value set (reported here, not written to the CSV). The same thinning rule as manhattan.csv was then applied to all four numeric columns together, keyed on the underlying p-value: kept all 21,835 points with p<1e-3, plus a seeded (numpy default_rng, seed 20150212) random sample of the remaining 2,533,250 points. Adding ci_lower/ci_upper doubled the column count from 2 to 4, so a 2% bulk rate (that fit qq.csv before the CI columns were added) rose to 1,993,992 bytes, 6 KB under the 2 MB cap and too tight a margin to trust; the bulk rate was reduced to 1.5% (37,938 sampled, 2,495,312 dropped) and the rounding precision reduced from 6 to 4 decimal places, giving 59,773 rows / 1,646,768 bytes with real headroom under the cap.
thinning: Keep the 2000 rows with the largest observed -log10 p, plus the row nearest to each of 1500 evenly spaced values of the expected -log10 p over the other rows (1498 distinct rows). Each kept row keeps its band columns ci_lower and ci_upper, and the kept rows keep the source order.

derivation: Read the gunzipped MAF (2,207 mutation rows, tab-separated, header on line 1, no #version comment line; columns include Hugo_Symbol, Tumor_Sample_Barcode, Variant_Classification, Protein_Change). Cohort size (total distinct Tumor_Sample_Barcode values in the MAF) = 193. Ranked genes by number of distinct mutated samples; took the top 20 (cutoff at 6 mutated samples, no tie at the 20/21 boundary). One row per (gene, sample) pair with >=1 mutation among the top-20 genes (325 rows). Added one placeholder row per sample with none of the top-20 genes mutated (34 of the 193 samples), gene set to the rank-1 gene FLT3 and variant_classification left empty, so every sample in the cohort has at least one row and a chart can render an empty/present column per sample; 325 + 34 = 359 rows total. Underlying data are TCGA open-access, de-identified, non-germline somatic mutation calls, public and citable per TCGA publication guidelines; maftools redistributes this file under its own MIT license (quoted above), which covers this reuse.

derivation: Filtered the MAF to Hugo_Symbol == DNMT3A (54 rows). Parsed aa_position with regex p\.\D*?(\d+) applied to Protein_Change (first run of digits after the non-digit prefix, so p.R882H -> 882, p.599_600insDFREYEY-style FLT3-style strings -> the first coordinate). 3 of 54 rows had a blank Protein_Change (Splice_Site calls with no annotated protein change) and were dropped; all other rows parsed. Grouped the remaining 51 rows by (aa_position, protein_change, variant_classification). R882 (p.R882H count=19, p.R882C count=7, p.R882P count=1) is the dominant hotspot, consistent with the published DNMT3A R882 pattern in AML.
